 Use of approved systems in alignment with company expectations.

 Job Description: 
 Are you passionate about computing and AI accelerators?
 Do you thrive on innovation and want to disrupt the industry? Are you eager to work with leading AI hardware engineers on Intel's latest architecture? If you love collaborating with diverse teams to create best-in-class AI compute platforms, Intel's GPE department has exciting opportunities for you.
 As a member of the GPE team, you will develop hardware and platform solutions for Intel products, including the newest IPs targeted at next-generation GPUs and AI accelerators. 
 You will have the opportunity to engage in enabling technologies in PCB design, manufacturing, testing, and debugging. We are a winning team with a clear vision of delivering competitive and cutting-edge products, and we are committed to building the best products and developing the best skills for our team.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Work on end-to-end power delivery design and development, from initial concept to implementation of power delivery requirements and ecosystem enabling power integrated circuits.
 Own power integrity simulation for the platform power delivery network: build and correlate VRM-to-die PDN models, run DC IR-drop and AC target-impedance analysis, and perform transient droop and Ldi/dt studies across die, package, and PCB to set the decoupling and stack up strategy before layout is committed.
 Apply knowledge of power conversion topologies, including components, compensation circuits/stability analysis, drop/droop analysis, simulation tools , and techniques, as well as PCB layout and design tools, to characterize performance and validate correlation of simulation modeling and results.
 Design and validate platform power conversion and management solutions, including energy management, and perform simulation and optimization for package and PCB, including stack up, power/ground noise plane assignment, decoupling solutions, and/or power sequencing requirements.
 Design for debug: architect observability into the board from the start, including per-rail voltage and current sense points, Kelvin-sense and probe landing points, telemetry and current-monitor access (SVID/PMBus/IMON), rail-level isolation and enable control, and voltage-margining , so power-on and post-silicon issues can be isolated on the first board instead of a respin.
 Design for flexibility: build configurability into the power delivery solution so a single board can support multiple SKUs and derivatives, using stuffing options for phase count and decoupling, pin-compatible dual-source regulator footprints, rail split/merge and current headroom for higher-power SKUs, and programmable load line, compensation, and VID range.
 Create and execute test plans to validate and characterize power delivery solutions.
 Correlate bench and VR test tool measurements with simulation results to improve simulation model accuracy and close the loop on power integrity assumptions.
 Conduct failure analysis and root cause investigations for power delivery issues, implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
 Collaborate with silicon and platform architects to generate solutions and analyses, delivering content into platform design guides as solution collaterals for end customers.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including board design, SW/FW, and systems validation, to ensure seamless integration of power delivery solutions.

 Minimum Qualifications , you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
 5+ years of experience in:
 Designing low voltage, high current, multi-phase DC-DC switching regulators (buck, boost, etc.) to meet stringent targets, optimizing the design for transient response and conversion efficiency. 
 Working with signal/power integrity and power delivery network simulation tools such as Cadence Sigrity PowerDC/PowerSI, Ansys SIwave etc. to develop accurate models of circuit design  
 Design and optimize accurate power delivery simulation models using SPICE and time-based simulation tools (LTSpice, SIMPLIS etc.) based on SOC design power requirements. 
 Power delivery network modeling across die, package, and PCB, including stackup, plane assignment, decoupling network design, and S-parameter extraction and correlation.
 Experience using oscilloscopes and DAQ for hardware troubleshooting and debugging.
 Interacting with Signal Integrity, Layout, and Mechanical engineers, with working knowledge of SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical aspects of board designs.
 Preferred Qualifications, are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.
 Experience designing for debug and testability on power delivery hardware, including sense and telemetry instrumentation, voltage margining, and rail isolation for post-silicon bring-up.
 Experience designing configurable power delivery solutions that support multiple SKUs and derivative products from a single board design.
 Identify new technologies/interfaces and develop board power delivery architecture.

 Experience delivering products for high-volume production and cost optimization.
 Knowledge of board and power management (HW/SW/FW) debugging.

 Portless is a tech-enabled supply chain business that helps DTC brands ship directly from Asia to customers worldwide in 5-9 days. We're transforming how ecommerce brands think about fulfillment by eliminating the traditional 60-90 day ocean freight model and replacing it with faster, more flexible, cash-flow friendly logistics.
 We're venture backed and growing fast. Our customers include brands shipping everything from apparel to consumer electronics, and we operate in 55+ countries. We're on a mission to make global fulfillment as seamless as domestic shipping.
 The Role
 We're looking for a Director of New Business Sales to lead the team of AEs responsible for winning new logos at Portless.
 You'll inherit a team of seven new business Account Executives selling into the SMB and Mid-Market segments, with ACVs most commonly associated with Enterprise deal values in other industries. These are real deals with real complexity: multiple stakeholders, operational diligence, and buyers who need to move physical product in order to go live with our solution. Your team owns those deals end-to-end, from qualified opportunity through implementation.
 This is a leadership role, not a player-coach role. You won't carry a personal quota. You will be measured on whether your team hits its number, and on whether the people on it get better while they do it. That means recruiting and retaining talent others want to hire, building a high-performance and low-ego culture, coaching at a world-class level, and knowing when to put your own hands on a deal.

 Recruit and retain outstanding sales talent. You'll own hiring for the new business team as we scale beyond seven AEs, build a bench before you need it, and keep your best people here and growing.

 Coach at a world-class level through call reviews, deal reviews, and 1:1s. You'll use our "One Thing" coaching philosophy to give each AE focused, specific feedback that measurably improves their craft.
 Get into the deals that matter. You'll bring real deal sense to your team's highest-potential opportunities, joining calls, shaping strategy, engaging senior stakeholders, and helping close business without taking the deal away from the rep.
 Own the number. You'll forecast accurately, track leading indicators, and diagnose pipeline problems early enough to do something about them.
 Run deal cycles across regions. You'll partner directly with our team in Asia and support your AEs on opportunities in Europe, Australia, and APAC.

 3+ years of sales leadership experience managing quota-carrying Account Executives.
 Your own track record as a quota-bearing closer in the mid-market and/or enterprise space.
 Demonstrated ability to recruit great sales talent and retain it.

 Demonstrated coaching ability, with specific examples of reps who measurably improved under you.
 A track record of winning deals yourself, and of helping your team win deals you were involved in.
 Comfort working across time zones, including direct collaboration with our team in Asia and deal cycles in Europe, Australia, and APAC.
 Experience with CRM and sales tools (HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, etc.).

 Experience selling to ecommerce, DTC, or retail brands.
 Familiarity with logistics, supply chain, 3PL, or fulfillment industry.
 Experience with usage-based pricing models.
 Experience scaling a sales team through a period of rapid headcount growth.
 Previous experience at a high-growth startup where you helped build the sales motion.

 Resilient: You navigate complex deals and setbacks without losing momentum.
 Driven: You're motivated by achievement and like to compete.
 Low-Ego: If you aren't a team player you will fail here.
 Why Portless

 Competitive compensation
 Equity
 Full benefits

The Toronto Star is seeking a skilled and driven journalist to join its Business and Housing team, covering the housing beat. Housing is one of the most urgent and consequential stories in Canada right now — touching affordability, development, tenant rights, municipal policy and the everyday lives of millions of Ontarians — and this reporter will be at the centre of it.
 The successful candidate will cover housing in all its dimensions: the politics of zoning and intensification, the struggles of renters and first-time buyers, the decisions of developers and city planners, the impact of interest rates and immigration on supply and demand, and the human stories behind the numbers. They will work closely with colleagues on the Business and Housing team and across the newsroom to produce journalism that is agenda-setting, accurate and deeply connected to the lives of Star readers in the GTA and beyond.
 This role sits within the Journalist classification in the Star's Editorial Department. While the initial assignment is to the housing beat within the Business and Housing team, journalists may be assigned across a variety of newsroom roles in the future. The position reports to the Senior Editor, Business and Housing.
 What you will do 
 Break and develop housing news across a broad range of topics — affordability, development, tenant rights, municipal policy, the rental market, real estate trends and the intersection of housing with broader economic and social issues.
 Generate original story ideas rooted in strong sourcing, data literacy and a genuine understanding of how housing issues affect real people across the GTA and Ontario.
 Build and maintain a deep network of sources — including city planners, developers, tenant advocates, municipal politicians, real estate economists, renters, buyers and industry insiders.
 Work collaboratively with colleagues on the Business and Housing team, as well as the visuals, multimedia and audience teams, to produce ambitious multi-platform storytelling.
 Produce a mix of daily news and longer-form enterprise and feature work, with strong written copy delivered accurately on deadline.
 Think beyond text — contributing ideas and content for video, audio and digital formats in collaboration with multimedia colleagues.
 Use data, public records and access-to-information requests to deepen and differentiate reporting.
 Maintain the Toronto Star's rigorous journalistic standards in all coverage.
Proven experience as a journalist at a daily news organization, with a track record of strong, original reporting.
 Demonstrated knowledge of or experience covering housing, real estate, urban affairs, municipal politics or related beats — or a clear and compelling case for how your reporting experience translates.
 Exceptional news judgment, writing skills and the ability to tell complex stories in ways that are clear, compelling and relevant to a broad readership.
 Strong source-building skills and the ability to work contacts across government, industry, advocacy groups and affected communities.
 Experience with data journalism, public records research and access-to-information requests — or a willingness to develop these skills.
 The ability to generate a steady stream of original, ambitious story ideas and see them through from pitch to publication.
 A self-starter mentality — able to manage multiple stories simultaneously, work independently and meet deadlines in a fast-paced newsroom.
 Comfort with digital storytelling and an understanding of how audiences consume journalism across platforms.
 Familiarity with CP style and a commitment to accuracy and fairness.
 A deep understanding of the GTA, its communities and the issues that matter most to people who live and work here.
 A demonstrated commitment to the Torstar values of collaboration, focus, selflessness, agility and results.
 Salary: $61,153.45 - $96,697.60

At Poka, we're changing how the world's industrial teams work — capturing the knowledge of their best people and putting it in every operator's hands.

 Poka is looking for a Web Strategist to own how our website gets found and how well it converts. Search is changing fast. Buyers now get answers from Google's AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and voice assistants as often as from a traditional results page. We need someone who understands both worlds: classic SEO and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), which means earning visibility and citations in AI-generated answers. Traffic is only half the job, so you'll also lead Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) to turn visitors into leads and customers.
 This is a strategic and hands-on role. You'll set direction, run experiments, and work closely with content, design, development, and demand generation to improve the website's performance.
 What you'll do 
 Search and answer engine strategy 
 Build and own an integrated SEO and AEO roadmap that grows organic visibility, qualified traffic, and brand presence in AI-generated answers.
 Run keyword, topic, and intent research, including the conversational and question-based queries people use with AI assistants, and turn it into content and site architecture plans.
 Structure content so answer engines can extract and cite it, using clear question-and-answer formatting, concise definitions, entity-rich copy, and comprehensive topic clusters.
 Implement and maintain structured data (Schema.org markup such as FAQ, HowTo, Product, Organization, and Article) to improve eligibility for rich results and AI citations.
 Monitor and improve how the Poka appears across AI platforms. Track mentions, citations, and share of voice in tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews.
 Strengthen E-E-A-T signals (experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trustworthiness) through author profiles, original research, and credible sourcing.
 Technical SEO 
 Conduct regular technical audits covering crawlability, indexation, site speed, Core Web Vitals, mobile experience, internal linking, canonicalization, and redirects.
 Work with the development team to prioritize and ship technical fixes, and make sure new pages and site changes are search-friendly from the start.
 Manage XML sitemaps, robots.txt directives, and crawler access policies, including decisions about AI crawlers.
 Conversion rate optimization 
 Own the CRO program from start to finish: find friction points, form hypotheses, design experiments, and report results.
 Plan and run A/B and multivariate tests on landing pages, forms, CTAs, navigation, pricing pages, and key user flows.
 Use analytics, heatmaps, session recordings, user surveys, and usability testing to understand how visitors behave and why they drop off.
 Work with design and copywriting teams to improve messaging, page layouts, and user experience based on test results and research.
 Build and maintain a testing backlog that is prioritized by expected impact and effort.
 Analytics and reporting 
 Define KPIs and build dashboards that track organic traffic, rankings, AI visibility, engagement, conversion rates, and pipeline or revenue attributed to the website.
 Deliver regular performance reports with clear insights and recommended next steps for leadership and stakeholders.
 Stay current on search algorithm updates, AI search developments, and CRO best practices, and adjust strategy as the landscape shifts.
 What you'll bring 
 Required 
 7+ years of experience in SEO, web strategy, or growth marketing, with measurable results in organic growth and conversion improvement.
 Deep knowledge of on-page, off-page, AEO, and technical SEO, and a solid working understanding of how large language models and AI search engines retrieve, summarize, and cite content.
 Proven experience running structured CRO programs, including test design, statistical significance, and turning results into action.

WANTED: One Hungry Closer Who's Sick Of Selling Other People's Dreams. 
 (Read this whole thing. If you quit halfway, we already have your answer.) 
 Most job ads read like they were written by HR. 
Bullet points. Buzzwords. 
A "competitive compensation package" that translates to "we'll pay you just enough to keep you from leaving, but never enough to actually win." 
 This isn't that.
 This is a letter. From us to you. About one of the most lopsided opportunities we've ever put in front of a salesperson and the rare, specific human being we're trying to find to fill it.
 If that human is you, you're going to feel it in your chest somewhere around paragraph nine.
 First — Who We Are. And Why It Matters. 
 We're Wealth Without Wall Street. 
 Russ Morgan and Joey Muré built this from scratch, not in a Manhattan glass tower, not with a hedge-fund pedigree, but by getting fed up watching hardworking business owners hand their financial futures to suit-wearing strangers who couldn't pick them out of a lineup.
 Together we've helped thousands of business owners, real estate investors, doctors, and high-earning professionals do what 99% of America has been brainwashed into believing is impossible:
 Generate passive income that exceeds their monthly expenses. 
 That's the whole game. That's what freedom actually looks like — not a 401(k) you can't touch until you're 65 and your knees are gone, but real cash flowing in every single month whether you work or not.
 We do it using the Infinite Banking Concept — the same wealth strategy quietly used by the richest families in America for over a century. We teach people to become their own bank. To recycle their capital. To stop renting money from institutions that profit off their ignorance.
 Russ and Joey have done it themselves. Over $50,000 per month in passive income. Co-authors of an Amazon bestseller. Hosts of one of the most respected podcasts in personal finance.
 This isn't theory. This is the real thing.
 Right now, we have more qualified people waving their hands than we can possibly talk to.
 That's where you come in.
 The Role: Business Developer. (Translation: The Person Who Decides Who Gets Free.) 
 Let us describe a typical day so you know exactly what you're signing up for.
 You wake up. You check your calendar. There are real, pre-qualified humans on it, people who registered for our workshops, devoured Russ and Joey's content, raised their hand, and said "I want a Passive Income Game Plan Session." 
 These aren't cold strangers. 
These aren't leads scraped off a list. 
These are people who already trust the brand, already believe the philosophy, and already know they're tired of the rat race.
 Your job is to pickup the phone, set appointments by making outbound calls and take inbound appointments.
Ask the kind of questions most salespeople are too soft to ask. 
Find out where they really are financially, emotionally, mentally. Diagnose whether IBC and our path is actually right for them.
 And if it is? You hand them the keys.
 You're not pitching. You're not pressuring. You're not chasing.
 You're the bridge between someone's current life — exhausted, overworked, financially fragile — and the version of their life where they sleep through the night because money is finally working for them instead of against them.
 That's the job.
 If that sounds like too much responsibility, the back button is right there.
 Who We Are NOT Looking For. 
 Let's save us both some time.
 We are not looking for the guy who calls himself a "closer" because he sold timeshares in Cabo for six months.
 We are not looking for the person who needs a six-week ramp, a personal coach, three resource Slack channels, and a "psychologically safe" environment to dial a phone.
 We are not looking for someone who's going to ghost on Friday afternoons because the surf is up.
 We are not looking for a salary chaser. If a guaranteed paycheck is what you're after, McDonald's is hiring. Go thrive.
 And we are definitely not looking for someone who can't speak from the heart about money, freedom, and the very real fear most Americans carry around about both. If you can't connect at the soul level, you can't sell this. Period.
 Who We ARE Looking For. 
 A killer. But a killer with a conscience.
 Someone who can sit across a Zoom screen from a stranger and — within ten minutes — have them admitting things they haven't told their spouse.
 Someone who's already a top performer somewhere else and is bored to tears selling SaaS, solar, or something else they couldn't care less about.
 Someone who reads Rich Dad Poor Dad , listens to BiggerPockets, follows Dave Ramsey just to argue with him, and already has an opinion about whole life insurance — even if that opinion needs updating.
 Someone with the spine to say "I don't think you're a fit. Here's why," and walk away from money on principle.
 Someone who treats every conversation like it's their last shot — because that's how the great ones do it.
 If you read those five paragraphs and felt seen, keep going.
 The Non-Negotiables.
 Proven sales background. Minimum 2+ years closing in a high-ticket, phone/Zoom-based environment. We don't care about your resume — we care about your numbers.
 25%+ close rate after probation. Below that, you're not the right fit and we'll part as friends.
 Full ownership of your pipeline. Nobody is going to chase you to follow up. The leads are there. The CRM is built. The systems work. You just have to work them. 
 Show up sharp every single day. This is a high-tempo environment. We move. We measure. We adjust.
 Live the message. If you don't believe building wealth outside the traditional system is possible, you cannot sell it. Period. Bonus points if you already own a whole life policy, have read Becoming Your Own Banker by Nelson Nash, or have personal experience with real estate investing or passive income.
 Stable, professional remote setup. High-speed internet, quiet environment, quality camera and mic. We're representing a premium brand on every single call.
 CRM discipline. You log notes the same day. You update statuses in real time. If "I forgot to update the CRM" is a phrase that comes out of your mouth more than twice, this won't work.
 Emotional intelligence over scripts. We'll give you frameworks. We will not give you a robot script to memorize. If you can't read a human, you can't sell here.
 Coachable ego. Strong opinions, loosely held. We promote killers who listen. We fire prima donnas who don't.
 A worldview that aligns. You believe people are responsible for their own freedom. You believe Wall Street is not the answer for most families. You believe in earning the right to be paid well — not waiting to be handed it.
 The Catch: 
 We get a lot of applications. 
Most won't make it past the first filter. 
We're not looking for a resume, we're looking for evidence. 
 A sales background that proves you can sit in the fire without flinching, a track record that doesn't need to be inflated, and a worldview that aligns with what we actually believe about money, freedom, and the responsibility of helping someone change their life.
 If that's you, apply. Right now. While you're feeling it.
 The Compensation. (Read This Slowly.) 
 We're going to lay this out plainly because we want you to do the math before you apply, not after.
 100% commission. Uncapped. No ceiling. No politics. 
 10% of cash collected on all Passive Income Lab Sales ($7,500 Price Point)
 20% of cash collected on all PIOS Sales ($1,000 Price Point)
 OTE for the people who actually do the work: $120K–$200K+ annually
 The top performers here aren't just closers. 
They're portfolio builders. 
Every month you close, you're stacking another stream of recurring income on top of what you closed last month. 
Twelve months in, you've got a book of business that pays you whether you take the call or not.
 Sound familiar?
 That's right. 
We pay you the same way we teach our clients to live. 
Passive income. Compounding. Freedom.
 If we wouldn't drink our own Kool-Aid with the people who sell our offer, we'd have no business selling it to anyone.
 What's In It For The Right Person. 
 Beyond the money?
 Mission that matters. You'll be the first conversation thousands of families ever have about real financial freedom. You'll be the one who makes them realize they've been lied to for thirty years, and you'll be the one who shows them the way out.
 Direct access to Russ Morgan and Joey Muré, two of the most generous, mission-driven, real-deal humans in this industry.
 Elite-level sales coaching from closers who've done eight figures in this exact niche.
 100% remote. From your kitchen. From Bali. From a coffee shop in Medellín. We don't care where the work happens. We care that the work happens.
 Pre-qualified, warm inbound leads — not cold lists, not scraped data, not random dials.
 A real product you can be proud of. No bait-and-switch. No fake scarcity. No "course that goes nowhere." A genuine pathway to freedom backed by a decade of results.

 Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. 
 Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

 Samsara is the industry leader in AI for physical operations. 
 We're hiring a Lead Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to serve as the technical anchor for ML infrastructure across Samsara's Safety AI organization. You will own the architecture and evolution of our end-to-end ML platform — spanning training, experimentation, inference, and edge deployment across more than 2M deployed devices — and be the connective tissue between applied ML teams, security, and data platform. This role is not an execution role sitting under a technical lead; you are the technical lead. Your decisions shape platform direction, unblock multiple product teams, and translate directly into real-world safety outcomes for the industries that run our world.

 In this role, you will: 
 ML Platform & Infrastructure 
 Set the technical strategy and own end-to-end delivery of Samsara's ML platform (training, experimentation, batch/online inference, edge) — making architectural decisions and being the accountability point across all platform layers for multiple Safety AI product teams. 
 Experimentation & Measurement 
 Drive the design, launch, and iteration of Safety AI features (CV models, EcoDriving insights, LLM-based reporting) — not just enabling others to ship, but co-owning outcomes including safety metrics, reliability, and cost at production scale. 
 Inference & Edge Deployment

 Reliability, Security & Operations

 Own or co-own end-to-end technical delivery for high-priority or high-risk initiatives, from modeling and system design through production rollout.

 Be the technical authority for ML infrastructure architecture across Safety AI — setting direction that cross-functional teams (applied ML, firmware, security, data platform) execute against, mentoring senior engineers and applied scientists, and ensuring platform decisions are made at the right level of abstraction with the right trade-offs.

 Hands-on Ray and Kubernetes expertise in production environments; Spark experience strongly preferred. Able to be a credible peer to the most senior engineers on the team. 
 Deep understanding of ML fundamentals beyond pipelines: evaluation methodology, dataset design, ablation, drift, and the ability to review and redirect modeling approaches — you bridge research and engineering, not just serve them.

Hi! I'm Daryl, and I'm the Manager of High Touch (Mid-Market) Implementations at Ashby. One of my favorite things about this team is that we're the first real proof point for a new customer; from day 1, we get the hands-on opportunity to show them why they made the right call switching to Ashby.

The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we added more than 2,100 new customers in the last year alone and now support over 5,000 customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. We're expecting similarly fast growth this year, and every one of those new customers needs a thoughtful implementation to actually get value out of Ashby. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're expanding this team!




THE ROLE:

We're looking for a Mid-Market Implementation Specialist who excels at leading technically complex, hands on implementation projects for B2B SaaS customers. You'll own each implementation from the moment Sales hands it off through go-live; part project manager, part technical expert, and part trusted advisor to the customer!

Six months in, success looks like carrying a full book of 15-20 active implementations, running each customer relationship on your own (kickoff, timeline, follow-through), independently solving complex configuration and workflow challenges, and handling the normal bumps (a slow-to-respond customer, a technical snag, an escalation) without the rest of your book slipping. It also means you're starting to make things better beyond your own accounts: you've found at least one process or documentation gap and fixed it, and you're feeding real customer feedback back to our Product team.




YOU WILL ACHIEVE THIS BY:

 - Managing 15-20 active mid-market implementations at a time (8-10 weeks implementation timeline on average), building each customer's project plan from handoff through go-live, and staying on top of timelines, hurdles, and follow-up along the way

 - Getting genuinely comfortable with the in’s and out’s of how our products work, so you can troubleshoot and advise instead of just walking through a checklist

 - Advising on what’s worked well for similar customers in the past, challenging assumptions when appropriate, and recommending configurations and workflows that balance customer needs with implementation best practices

 - Partnering closely with cross-functional partners across the business, especially Sales and CS to ensure a seamless customer journey, and Product/Engineering to flag real issues and align on a path forward

As you're probably gathering, we're looking for someone who gets energy from both sides of this: the structure of running a tight project plan, and the judgment to rethink that plan when a customer's business genuinely calls for it.



If you have the majority of the following, you could be a great fit for this role: 

 - 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing role, with the majority of your focus on leading full-cycle B2B SaaS implementations

 - Proven track record successfully managing concurrent mid-market implementation projects without compromising quality, customer experience, or timelines

 - Experience operating with real autonomy and to own the implementation project plans end-to-end

 - Comfortable getting into the weeds of complex, multi-module software, and building genuine fluency in how it all fits together

 - Resourceful when there's no documented answer; you do your own testing and discovery, then use what you learn to advise customers on best practices and recommendations

 - Data-driven and detail-oriented, with a genuine instinct for coaching customers through unfamiliar territory

If you need someone else to do any of the following, then this role is probably not for you:

 - Independently investigate complex customer questions and become the technical/product subject matter expert during implementations

 - Carry more than a handful of accounts at once (this is a high volume role on a team that moves with urgency)

 - Own the execution of a project plan, not just its design

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

 - We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly.

 - We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager, Automations Platform to be part of our AI Workflows product organization.



The team:

The Automations Platform team builds the system that lets Jobber Teammate, our AI teammate for home service businesses, do a service provider's work for them. Every automation in Jobber runs on what this team builds.



The role:

You'll make it possible for Jobber Teammate to automate every task in Jobber.

Today a handful of automations exist and each one is expensive to build. The ambition is that every task a service provider repeats in their week has an automation that does it for them. Getting there takes two things at once, and this role does both.

You'll build the platform: the authoring, execution and evaluation models that let any product team at Jobber ship an automation without first becoming AI specialists. Skill files, tool calls, and evals that make an automation measurably better over time.

You'll also build on the platform: choosing the automations that matter most, shipping them yourself, and making them easy to find, enable and trust. Being the platform's hardest customer is what keeps it honest.

Over time you'll open it up, so service providers create their own and the best ones spread to businesses like theirs.

This suits someone equally at home in an architecture discussion and a customer interview.



As Senior Product Manager you will:

 - Build a deep understanding of home service businesses and the repeated work that consumes their week.

 - Own the automation platform: how automations are authored, how they execute, and how they're evaluated and improved.

 - Make it fast and cheap for any Jobber team to ship an automation, and measure yourself on their throughput rather than your own.

 - Build the highest-impact automations yourself, and make them easy for service providers to find, enable and trust.

 - Build an Evals platform, that makes it easy to iterate on and improve automations so the quality bar is constantly raising

 - Bring the product requirements to our AI Foundations engineering team, who build the underlying agent infrastructure.

 - Define the metrics that tell you the platform works: cost and speed of building an automation, engagement with the ones we ship, and growth of the library.

 - 5+ years of product management experience, with evidence of shipping real AI products and seeing them through to long-term outcomes.

 - A growth mindset and someone who thrives in change and ambiguity. The AI Org you’ll join is a fast moving space and we expect that the technology, positioning, scope and roles will all continue to evolve as we learn together

 - Experience building an AI platform was genuinely adopted - won through advocacy, tooling, and documentation.

 - Experience shipping LLM-backed or ML-backed products, with real respect for how they fail.

 - A track record of making a contested technical decision and making it stick.

 - Comfort thinking in unit economics, because the cost of building an automation decides whether this strategy is real.

 - Experience with agent frameworks, tool calling, or evaluation and observability systems for AI.

 - Experience with workflow automation, or no-code and low-code builder products.

 - Experience in home services, field service, or SMB software.

 Define architecture and set technical direction for projects.
 Lead project teams, mentoring and guiding multiple designers to ensure high-quality outcomes.

 Degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent.

 Familiarity with device driver development for Linux and real-time OSes.

 Skills in HW/SW/FPGA integration and debugging using schematics, datasheets, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.
 Strength in object-oriented design principles and implementation.
 Knowledge of scripting languages such as Python, Bash, and TCL.

 Strong technical leadership, emphasizing quality design practices.

About Skillshare 
 Skillshare is an online learning community whose mission is to connect curious, lifelong learners everywhere – and, in so doing, build a more creative, more generous, and more prosperous world. Today, our community has grown to millions of members who come to Skillshare to learn creative and entrepreneurial skills, network with peers, and even teach a class themselves. We are backed by OMERS Growth Equity, Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, Amasia, Spero Ventures, and Burda Principal Investments.
 Skillshare is committed to building a diverse team that reflects a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We work to ensure a consistent interview process, and inclusive work environment for all.
 About the role 
 As an engineer at Skillshare, you'll help shape how teachers share their expertise, how students discover and watch content they love, and how our platform evolves for the future. This role sits at the foundation of our backend, including our domain model, service architecture, event backbone, and the conventions other engineers build on top of.
 We work in a TypeScript monorepo built around Domain-Driven Design, hexagonal architecture, and Clean Architecture principles. Our services are built with NestJS, our API is GraphQL, our data lives in Postgres behind Prisma, and our infrastructure runs on GCP.
 We're looking for someone who thinks deeply about systems and boundaries, is comfortable making and documenting architectural decisions, and can leave behind a codebase that other engineers can understand and build upon.
 AI is also a core part of how our engineering team works. We use tools like Claude Code throughout the development process, and we're looking for someone who knows how to effectively direct, review, and improve AI-generated work while remaining accountable for the architecture, quality, and end result.
 What You'll Do: 
 Shape our backend architecture and domain model , defining clear bounded contexts, aggregates, domain events, and service boundaries that reflect how the business actually works.
 Build and evolve TypeScript/NestJS services using Domain-Driven Design and ports-and-adapters patterns, keeping business logic isolated from infrastructure.
 Own key backend contracts , including our GraphQL API, Postgres data models, and the patterns we use to evolve them safely as the product grows.
 Build reliable event-driven systems , designing for durability, idempotency, retries, and the realities of distributed systems.
 Use an AI coding harness as a core development tool , directing and reviewing generated code while improving the context, standards, tests, and guardrails that make AI-assisted development more effective.
 Raise the bar for engineering quality through thoughtful code review, testing, technical documentation, architecture diagrams, and clear decision records.
 Turn ambiguous product needs into well-designed systems, partnering with product and engineering teammates to model problems, make tradeoffs, and ship meaningful work.
 Work within our weekly delivery cadence , breaking foundational work into meaningful increments that can move from Monday goals to Friday demos.
 8+ years of experience building backend systems in production, with deep TypeScript and Node.js experience and the judgment that comes from owning and maintaining systems you've designed.
 Deep, hands-on experience with Domain-Driven Design . You've applied DDD to real, complex domains and are comfortable defining bounded contexts, aggregate boundaries, value objects, and domain events. You understand hexagonal architecture / ports and adapters, including both the value of that separation and when the additional indirection is worth it.
 Strong experience designing and owning GraphQL APIs , including schema modeling, batching and the N+1 problem, pagination, error semantics, and evolving a live schema without breaking clients.
 Experience designing event-driven and distributed systems . You can reason concretely about at-least-once delivery, idempotency, ordering, retries, transactional boundaries, and patterns such as the transactional outbox.
 Strong relational data modeling and SQL fundamentals , including schema design, migrations against live data, indexing, transaction boundaries, and designing read and write paths intentionally.
 Experience with NestJS or significant production experience in another modern Node.js backend framework such as Fastify, Express, Hono, AdonisJS, or tRPC, with the ability to ramp quickly on NestJS.
 You're highly proficient with AI coding tools such as Claude Code or a comparable agentic coding harness. AI isn't occasional autocomplete in your workflow. You're comfortable directing an agent through meaningful engineering work while owning the architecture, context, review, and final result. You review generated code critically and know how to catch plausible-but-wrong implementations, missed edge cases, and broken invariants.
 You have strong testing instincts . You know how to design systems that are testable at the domain level, use fast implementations or test doubles appropriately, and reserve integration testing for the seams where systems actually integrate.
 You communicate technical decisions exceptionally well in writing and visually . Architecture decision records, domain glossaries, system diagrams, data and event flows, and technical standards are part of how you work, not documentation you add after the fact.
 You operate with a high degree of autonomy . You can take an ambiguous product or technical problem, model it, make thoughtful architectural tradeoffs, sequence the work, and drive it through completion without waiting for a fully written spec.
 You can maintain working-hour overlap with our US-based team until at least 1:00 PM Eastern each day. This is when much of our live collaboration happens, including code review, pairing, Monday goal-setting, and Friday demos. Outside of that window, we work largely asynchronously, so strong written communication and leaving clear context behind are important.
 Nice to Haves: 
Our current stack includes NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, Prisma, GCP, Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Pulumi, Nx, Bun, and Zod . You don't need to have worked with every tool in our stack. We're more interested in strong architectural fundamentals and experience with comparable technologies, but familiarity with several of these is a plus.
 We'd also be excited about experience with:
 Building or shaping codebases specifically for AI coding agents, including context files, agent rules, MCP servers, hooks, or automated development guardrails.
 Fine-grained authorization or relationship-based access control systems such as OpenFGA, Zanzibar-style ReBAC, or OPA.
 Running transactional outbox patterns, change data capture, or stream processing in production.
 Infrastructure as Code and cloud-native deployment environments.
 Monorepo architecture, developer tooling, generators, or custom plugins.
 Schema-driven contracts and runtime validation.
 Why You Are Excited About Us 
 Our team : We have a passionate, creative, and innovative team that is a lot of fun to work with.
 Our mission : We’re doing work that matters – connecting lifelong learners around the world and empowering them to pursue their creativity.
 Flexibility : We believe that doing your best work means living a full life. That means different things for everyone, so we optimize for trust, invest to support remote teams, offer home office stipends and co-working spaces in multiple cities, have an unlimited vacation policy (with a required minimum!), and encourage work-life balance.
 Impact : Your work will directly influence how millions of learners discover and engage with Skillshare.
 Your growth : You’ll have opportunities to collaborate across marketing, brand, product, and engineering teams while expanding your marketing design expertise.
 Benefits : We believe that doing your best work means living a full life. We support our team with unlimited PTO, gender-neutral parental leave, anniversary sabbaticals, and healthy stipends for creativity, learning, and personal wellness.
 At Skillshare, we believe creativity thrives in an inclusive environment. We're excited to meet candidates from all backgrounds and experiences. If you're passionate about what we do but don't check every single box, we'd still love to hear from you — curiosity and growth matter most to us.

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
 The autonomous transition is a transformational opportunity for Lyft. Our strategy focuses on becoming the preferred marketplace, fleet, and operational partner for the world's best Autonomous Vehicle (AV) providers. As AV deployments scale across new markets, the operational infrastructure that enables safe, compliant, and high-quality service becomes a critical competitive advantage. This role sits at the heart of that infrastructure - owning the systems, processes, and partner alignment that allow Lyft to operate at the standards our AV partners require and our riders expect.
 As a qualified candidate, you have a track record of building and running complex operational programs in highly regulated or standards-driven environments. You are energized by cross-functional complexity - comfortable leading structured implementation processes that span many teams while keeping a clear eye on compliance and quality outcomes. You bring a program management mindset, strong stakeholder communication skills, and the judgment to navigate ambiguity in a fast-moving industry.
 Responsibilities: 
 Own execution of AV partner audits end-to-end. That includes evidence collection, submission, partner and third-party review, mitigation oversight, and closeout, across concurrent certification cycles for multiple markets and AV partners, domestic and international.
 Act as a strategic leader within the company to support cross-functional teams’ compliance controls and readiness for partner scrutiny
 Drive coordination across teams including EHS, Legal, Safety, HR, IT and Operations for every deliverable. Translate partner and regulatory requirements into concrete, assignable asks and ensure deadlines are met
 Maintain and continuously improve the audit tracking system, including the evidence library, audit trail, and submission tooling. Lead platform improvements as volume and complexity grow
 Identify non-conforming items surfaced during audits, assist in identifying mitigation, and track corrective actions with the owning function through to closure
 Manage the logistics and stakeholder prep for audits, including document readiness and staff interviews 
 Build repeatable playbooks so each new market or partner audit cycle runs faster and with less rework than the last
 Report clearly and credibly on timelines and risk to leadership on behalf of AV Operational Excellence
 Act as the primary audit point of contact for AV partners 
 Experience: 
 5+ years in program management, compliance, quality assurance, or audit-adjacent roles within a regulated or standards-driven environment
 A track record of driving structured, deadline-driven cross-functional work without formal authority over contributing teams. Comfortable pushing partners to deliver and escalating when needed
 Strong command of audit and evidence management mechanics: tracking systems, documentation rigor, version control, and chain-of-custody type discipline
 Experience with spreadsheet or database-driven tracking systems, and interest in modernizing them
 Prior exposure to AV, automotive, aviation, or another safety-critical, audited industry strongly preferred
 This is an individual contributor role at launch, with room to grow into leading a small team as certification volume scales

 Position Summary 
 The Principal Medical Writer is a seasoned expert who owns complex safety writing deliverables end-to-end. In this role, they independently lead the authoring of high-impact safety documents—such as aggregate reports and Risk Management Plans (RMPs)—translating complex safety data and analyses into clear, compelling outputs. They are accountable for driving timelines, managing stakeholders, and ensuring the quality of safety deliverables that address important safety issues. Beyond day-to-day delivery, this role is a key champion for continuous improvement, best practices, and the smart adoption of new tools and technologies in the safety writing space.
 Responsibilities 
 This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:
 Independently lead preparation of complex clinical and post-market safety documents (e.g., DSURs, PSURs/PBRERs, ACOs, PADERs/PAERs, RMPs, and responses to regulatory authority questions), with strong hands-on experience across all key aggregate safety documents.
 Operate effectively within a global, complex matrix organization, working autonomously and confidently influencing stakeholders on process discipline, quality standards, and “how” work should be done.
 Lead cross-functional teams to develop content strategy, coordinate contributions, manage review schedules and timelines, and ensure high-quality, fit-for-purpose documents that accurately reflect safety, clinical, and statistical data and meet GSK and global/regional/local regulatory requirements.
 Provide oversight to co-authors, vendor writers, and teams of writers—serving as a mentor/buddy, ensuring the quality of contributions, and leading initiatives to improve medical writing processes, including effective use of authoring/review tools and other automation/AI-enabled technology platforms.
 Why You? 
 This role is hybrid. You will work on-site in Canada part of the week and remotely the remainder. Exact on-site days will be agreed with your manager.
 Basic Qualifications 
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals
 Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, health sciences, pharmacy, nursing or a related field.
 Minimum 5 years of advanced medical/regulatory safety writing experience in pharmaceutical, biotech or clinical research settings, including summarization and interpretation of complex data and independent preparation of complex clinical and safety documents for regulatory use.
 Advanced understanding of, and ability to apply, statistical, regulatory and medical communication concepts needed to independently write complex safety documents.
 In-depth working knowledge of relevant regulatory guidance (e.g., ICH, GVP, FDA, EMA) pertaining to clinical trial conduct, pharmacovigilance, and document-specific requirements, as well as Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
 Strong understanding of core cross-functional clinical research roles and procedures (e.g., safety, regulatory, clinical, epidemiology, statistics and programming) and how they relate to document strategy and operational preparation.
 Experience across multiple therapeutic areas, with confidence to quickly dive into new areas without extensive lead time.
 Proven ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced, global/matrix environment, working autonomously while effectively influencing stakeholders.
 Strong written and verbal English communication skills and excellent attention to detail.
 Preferred Qualifications 
If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus
 Advanced degree (PhD, PharmD, MSc, MPH) or equivalent scientific training.
 Advanced safety writing skills with expertise across most key safety document types and experience leading regulatory submission projects or preparing dossier modules.
 Comfort interpreting statistical outputs and collaborating with statisticians on tables and data displays.
 Highly collaborative and capable of leading cross-functional, multicultural, and hybrid/distributed teams across regions—negotiating solutions, advising on document structure and content, and working effectively with diverse stakeholders (e.g., health authorities, external partners, contractors/CROs, and patients).
 Experience working with external partners, contractors or clinical research organizations, including vendor oversight and coordination.
 Prior mentoring, training or people development experience, supporting the growth of less experienced writers and team members.
 Able to independently lead multiple projects simultaneously and deliver multiple high-quality documents on schedule.
 Advanced computer skills and general computer literacy, including comfort with collaboration tools and remote-working technologies.
 Excellent English language proficiency, both verbal and written.
 What you will gain 
You will join a team focused on patient impact and continuous learning. You will develop technical and strategic skills in regulatory writing, submission planning and cross-functional collaboration. Your work will shape development programs and contribute to better outcomes for patients.
 Ready to apply? 
If this role fits your skills and ambition, we want to hear from you. Please apply and tell us how your experience will help shape treatments that matter.
 #LI-Hybrid
 Skills 
Clinical Development, Clinical Trial Designs, Communication, Customer Service, Decision Making, Emotional Intelligence, Influencing Without Authority, Learning Agility, Literature Reviews, Medical Writing, Pharmaceutical Industry, Presentation Techniques, Regulatory Submissions, Scientific Writing, Strategic Thinking

 Posting Information:

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose 
 The primary objective of the position is to promote engineering innovation and entrepreneurship growth to exceed Faculty targets by raising the profile of research, initiating, developing, and maintaining industry relationships, and ensuring more research funding, in part by focusing on industry collaborations and partnership grant opportunities. The Director serves a vital end-to-end function in the growth, promotion, advancement, and management of engineering innovation and entrepreneurship activity on and off-campus and within the local and international entrepreneurship ecosystem, encompassing five key accountabilities:
 Planning and implementing new and ongoing innovation and entrepreneurship initiatives as part of the Engineering Research Office team.
 Participating directly in envisioning, initiating, and developing successful proposals for major research partnerships and initiatives, usually involving teams in collaboration with industry partners and other external stakeholders.
 Facilitating the establishment and success of research entities and strategic networks and supporting their growth through industry partnerships and interdisciplinary research.
 Developing industry relationships and successfully completing agreements for industry funding, in collaboration with the Office of Research, or building on opportunities arising from the efforts of Advancement and Development Officers within the Faculty and centrally, as part of large grant initiatives in strategic research areas.
 Provide leadership and direction in strategic planning to advance Engineering research as a top prospect at organizations that support commercialization and entrepreneurship, both within the University of Waterloo (UW) and outside and facilitate researchers’ access to such organizations.
 Key Accountabilities 
 Guide and support research, innovation and entrepreneurship growth and raise the 
 Faculty of Engineering profile to advance the faculty’s strategic research agenda, including but not limited to: 
 Provide leadership and direction in strategic planning activities to increase research, with a focus on highlighting its relevance to industry, and to advance innovation and entrepreneurship in the Faculty of Engineering in the short- and long-term. Work closely with the Associate Dean, Research and External Partnerships (ADR) and the Office of Research  to define and advance faculty research goals; in this capacity, the director monitors and evaluates progress against proposed objectives, identifies gaps in performance and capacity, and develops strategies to align Faculty priorities and exceed Faculty targets.
 Develop and oversee implementation of faculty- and department-level strategic recommendations, including communicating the Faculty’s strategies to encourage increased research funding, external research collaborations, and access to the entrepreneurship ecosystem.
 Work closely with the ADR to identify and develop opportunities to establish new research initiatives and grow existing programs. This includes increasing, strengthening and diversifying research funding sources, developing strategies to improve success rates in major federal and provincial award programs, and maintaining a working knowledge of significant developments and trends related to national and global economics, innovation, and technological development to ensure research programs are strategically positioned to respond to emerging issues. Work with the ADR to understand and connect the Engineering Faculty to University and local technology association initiatives to support entrepreneurship, including Conrad School of Business and Entrepreneurship, WatCo, Velocity, the Accelerator Centre and Communitech.
 Solicit and orchestrate direct funding opportunities from government ministries at both the provincial and federal levels.
 Manage relationships within the research community on campus, as well as interactions with external financial partners, industry, academia, and alumni.
 Leading business and financial planning to establish viable strategic, tactical, and operational targets in close collaboration with the ADR.
 Work closely with the development and communications teams to develop and maintain a clear and integrated strategic communications plan to increase visibility of research within the Faculty of Engineering and influence stakeholders.
 Work with the development and communications teams to identify Engineering research success stories, organize funding announcements and media events, develop and produce materials to promote research programs and activities, and grow the Faculty of Engineering research ‘brand’.
 Communicate potential research opportunities to departments and individual faculty researchers and assessing their viability for possible follow-up.
 Provide leadership to individual researchers, support development and ongoing success of major research proposals, including but not limited to: 
 Identify opportunities for major research projects, including sources of funding, potential internal team members (taking interdisciplinary collaboration initiatives into account), and external industry partners who might sponsor or use the research, as well as non-industry partners and stakeholders.
 Provide guidance and direction in preparation, coordination, implementation and reporting on major funding proposals. This may involve acting as a de-facto member of the research team to ensure the development of a high-quality proposal.
 Provide guidance and coordinate efforts related to financial and technical reporting on major projects, assisting with internal and external audits.
 Establish and communicate internal deadlines for submission and review of research proposals to department chairs, faculty, and centres/institutes.
 Develop and distribute reference material to aid proposal development.
 Organize and chair in-house workshops, information sessions, and panel discussions on upcoming government/industries funding opportunities. This includes securing relevant agency and industry speakers to instruct faculty researchers on program guidelines and proposal development.
 Conduct final reviews of applications to ensure compliance with agency evaluation criteria and university guidelines, including budgets. This includes advising the ADR on proposal quality and likelihood of success.
 Coach and mentor faculty researchers in approaching, securing and extending industry partnerships.
 Provide leadership and strategic oversight for high-profile and mission-critical funding programs within the Faculty, including the Ontario Research Fund, Canada Foundation for Innovation
 programs, and other major federal and provincial initiatives. Serve as a trusted advisor to faculty members and staff on strategic funding opportunities, institutional competitiveness, and the effective communication of research impact to sponsors and stakeholders.
 Encourage researchers to be aware of, and apply for, awards administered by the ADR and external awards.
 Develop and maintain external partnerships, including but not limited to: 
 Initiate and cultivate meaningful and productive interactions with prospective industry, academic, and government partners. This includes delivering the Engineering research value proposition, helping potential partners identify and articulate a business problem, then connecting them with engineering and entrepreneurship research talent on campus who can provide research support.
 Cultivate long-term relationships to understand the industry partners’ business and challenges, to anticipate the partners’ needs which our researchers can fill and describe those opportunities in larger grants and other supporting documentation.
 Prepare draft agreements tailored to the specifics of a given research collaboration with a company or other partners.
 Liaise with the Office of Research to initiate and manage research agreements, including facilitating the resolution of disputes related to contractual terms, conditions, or requirements.
 Steward existing relationships, including managing and growing partnerships and tracking outcomes.
 Coordinate and provide direction to UW Industrial Liaison Officers, departments/school, and Faculty liaison staff to build an effective network of industry partnerships.
 Collaborate with development and alumni affairs teams within and outside the Faculty, to ensure relationships with current and potential supporters include research collaboration and sponsorship wherever possible.
 Coordinate and participate in campus visits, events, workshops, and conferences that bring together potential partners and Faculty of Engineering researchers.
 Ensure commercialization and entrepreneurship: 
 Guide and facilitate individual faculty, labs and research groups in accessing pathways for commercialization and entrepreneurship.
 ·Share best practices and experiences of others in protecting their intellectual property and exploiting it through commercialization.
 Participate in activities in the entrepreneurship ecosystem, including Conrad School of Business and Entrepreneurship, WatCo, Velocity, the Accelerator Centre and Communitech, to keep research in the Faculty of Engineering “top of mind” at these organizations, and to continuously update researchers in Engineering about the opportunities to benefit through initiatives at these organizations including partnerships, start-ups, and collaborative laboratories.
 Required Qualifications 
 Master’s degree required; doctoral degree, Master of Business Administration, or MBET (Master of Business, Entrepreneurship and Technology) degree strongly preferred.
 5-10 years in research administration, including experience in research commercialization and industry partnerships. Experience in an academic institution is preferred.
 Proven experience building relationships and establishing strong connections within local and international entrepreneurship ecosystems.
 Effective communication skills (both written and oral), including the ability to prepare and deliver presentations to large, diverse audiences.
 Outstanding interpersonal skills, including the ability to manage both internal and external relationships. The incumbent must have the ability to move seamlessly within academic, business, industrial, and governmental communities, being equally comfortable with students, faculty researchers, senior executives from small, medium, and large, multinational corporations, and government officials.
 Strong managerial skills, including the ability to manage and motivate personnel.
 Proven leadership skills, including the ability to define and implement strategic plans for advancement of large programs, and to build collaborative research opportunities with diverse groups.
 Excellent analytical skills and business acumen, including the ability to identify and articulate significant trends affecting economic, social, and environmental priorities and how they will impact innovation and technologies development.
 Effective critical thinking and decision-making skills.
 Ability to prepare and manage a complex budget.
 Ability to balance competing demands on tight deadlines within a results-oriented environment.
 Advanced knowledge and proficiency in a Microsoft Office Environment.
